officials.summary: Hassan II was King of Morocco from 1961 until his death in 1999. Hassan was born in Rabat during the reign of his father, Mohammed V, who would later lead Morocco to independence from French and Spanish rule.

aliases: Puno ime : Mohamed V Abdelhamad-Shorta Sidi Ben Jousef of Morocco
officials.summary: Muhammad V was the ruler of Morocco from 1927 to 1961, except for a two-year period in exile during the 1950s. He reigned as sultan until 1957, and afterwards as the first king of Morocco.

Mohammed VI is King of Morocco, reigning since 1999. A member of the Alawi dynasty, Mohammed was born during the reign of his father, King Hassan II. At an early age, he began partaking in public engagements on behalf of his father.

Abbas El Fassi is a Moroccan politician and businessman who served as the Prime Minister of Morocco from 19 September 2007 to 29 November 2011. El Fassi, a member of the Istiqlal Party, replaced independent Driss Jettou.

Abdallah Ibrahim was a Moroccan politician and a figure of the national movement who served as the left-wing Prime Minister of Morocco between 16 December 1958, and 20 May 1960. He was the third Prime Minister of Morocco and served under king Mohammed V. He also served as the foreign minister from 1958 to 1960.

Abdelilah Benkirane is a Moroccan politician who served as Prime Minister of Morocco from 2011 to 2017. He has been secretary-general of the Justice and Development Party since 2021, having previously held the position from 2008 to 2017.

Abderrahmane Youssoufi was a Moroccan politician and human rights lawyer who served as Prime Minister of Morocco from 1998 to 2002, serving under King Hassan II and King Mohammed VI. He was the Secretary General of the Socialist Union of Popular Forces (French: Union Socialiste des Forces Populaires, USFP).

officials.party: Front for the Defence of Constitutional Institutions
officials.summary: Ahmed Bahnini was a Moroccan politician who served as the Prime Minister of Morocco from 1963 to 1965 under King Hassan II. He also served as President of the Supreme Court. Bahnini was killed during a failed coup attempt against Hassan II on 10 July 1971.
Ahmed Balafrej was the Prime Minister of Morocco between May 12, 1958, and December 2, 1958. He was a significant figure in the struggle for the independence of Morocco.
Ahmed Osman is a Moroccan lawyer and retired politician who served as the Prime Minister of Morocco from 1972 to 1979.

Aziz Akhannouch is a Moroccan politician, businessman, and billionaire who served as the Prime Minister of Morocco from 2021 to 2026. He served as Minister of Agriculture from 2007 to 2021 and is also the CEO of Akwa Group.

Azzeddine Laraki was a Moroccan politician who served as the Prime Minister of Morocco from 1986 to 1992. He was the tenth prime minister and served under king Hassan II. He later served as Secretary-General of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference (OIC) from 1997 to 2000, the first Moroccan to hold that position.
Driss Jettou is a Moroccan politician, who served as prime minister of Morocco from 2002 to 2007.
Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri (born 3 January 1976) is a Moroccan politician and lawyer who is the prime minister of Morocco since 29 September 2026. She is the first woman to hold the office.
Politician.

Maati Bouabid was a politician and a lawyer who served as the Prime Minister of Morocco between March 22, 1979, and November 30, 1983. He was the ninth Prime Minister of Morocco and served under king Hassan II. He also served as the Minister of Labor and Social Affairs from 1968 to 1970 and Minister of Justice.
Mbarek Bekkay Lahbil was the first Prime Minister of Morocco between December 7, 1955, and April 15, 1958. Bekkay held the rank of colonel in the French army.

Mohammed Karim Lamrani was a Moroccan politician who was the Prime Minister of Morocco for three separate terms. He served his first term for one year which started in 1971 and ended in 1972, then from November 1983 to September 1986, and finally from August 1992 to May 1994.

Saadeddine Othmani, sometimes transliterated as Saad Eddine el-Othmani, is a Moroccan politician and psychiatrist who served as the Prime Minister of Morocco from 2017 to 2021. Previously he served as foreign minister from 2012 to 2013.
Abdellatif Filali was a Moroccan politician and diplomat who was Prime Minister of Morocco from 1994 to 1998.

Abdellatif Loudyi (Arabic: عبد اللطيف لودييي) is a Moroccan civil servant and politician who has served as Minister Delegate to the Head of Government in charge of National Defense Administration (de facto defense minister) since 2010. He succeeded Abderrahmane Sbai in that position.
Abdelouahed Belkeziz, was a Moroccan lawyer, politician, and diplomat. He served as the eighth Secretary-General of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference (OIC) from 2001 to 2004.

Abderrahmane Sbai was a Moroccan politician and civil servant who was Minister Delegate to the Head of Government, in charge of National Defense Administration from 1997 to 2010. He held a degree in "geographic engineering".

Moulay Ahmed Laraki was a Moroccan politician and a figure of the national movement and served as the Prime Minister of Morocco from October 7, 1969, to August 6, 1971, under King Hassan II. He also served as the foreign minister from 1967 to 1971.
Moroccan politician.

M'hamed Boucetta (in Arabic: امحمد بوستة – Born 23 December 1925 in Marrakech – Dead 17 February 2017 in Rabat) was a Moroccan politician and lawyer. Boucetta held several top political position in post-independent Morocco, including: Minister of Justice (1961–1963), Minister of Foreign Affairs (1977–1979, 1979–1983) and co-founder and secretary general of the Istiqlal Party (1974–1998).

Mahjoubi Aherdane was a Moroccan politician, Amazigh nationalist, poet and painter. Alongside Abdelkrim al-Khatib, he founded the Popular Movement in 1957, a political party defending the Amazigh cause and formed mainly of former militants of the Moroccan Liberation Army (ALN).
Mohamed Benaissa was a Moroccan politician who served as the Minister of Foreign Affairs from 1999 to 2007.
Mohamed Taiyba Benhima was the Prime Minister of Morocco, serving from 7 July 1967 to 7 October 1969. He was born in Safi (Asfi) to Taïbi Benhima and Rkia Benhida.

Mohammed ben Mizzian was a Moroccan senior military officer and prominent military figure in Francoist Spain and Morocco. During the Spanish Civil War he commanded a unit of the Regulares Indígenas (Indigenous Regular Forces) troops, who formed the shock troops of the Nationalist faction.

General Mohamed Oufkir was a Moroccan senior military officer who held many important governmental posts like the minister of interior and minister of defense. Throughout the 60s, he rose to become the regime's strongman having a close relationship with Hassan II of Morocco and was partly responsible for the suppression of political opposition and riots.
Moroccan politician.
Nasser Bourita (Arabic: ناصر بوريطة; born (1969-05-27)27 May 1969) is a Moroccan diplomat serving as the Minister of Foreign Affairs, African Cooperation and Moroccan Expatriates since 5 April 2017.
Salaheddine Mezouar (Arabic: صلاح الدين مزوار – born 11 December 1953, Meknes) is a Moroccan politician and economist who served as Minister of Foreign Affairs from 10 October 2013 until 2017.

Taieb Fassi Fihri (born 9 April 1958) is a Moroccan politician who is Counselor to King Mohammed VI since January 2, 2012. Previously, he served in all successive governments between 1993 and 2012, first as Secretary of State and subsequently as Minister of Foreign Affairs.
Minister of foreign affairs for Morocco.
